title: The Impossible Transmitter

features.name: antenna grid
features.desc-on-touch: Rows of transmitter spires stretch into the node's distance, CP437 glyphs in pale blue, each one broadcasting into a void that never answers back.

features.name: broadcast tower
features.desc-on-touch: A skeletal wireframe tower, rotating slowly, sending the same message outward every three seconds. The message is just static. Has been for forty years.

features.name: equipment shed
features.desc-on-touch: A prefab shelter houses radios that listen only to their own transmissions, recording their own silence in an eternal loop.

features.name: carrier wave chamber
features.desc-on-touch: An underground chamber where the continuous low hum lives—the sound beneath the broadcast, the frequency that tries to say 'I am here' to nothing at all.

features.name: log cabinet
features.desc-on-touch: A filecard index, rows of broadcast logs. Each page marked: 'no reply received.' The handwriting never changes across decades.

inscription: here the archive learned what it meant to broadcast into the unmapped parts of itself

file.name: Broadcast_Log_Eastward_1981-2024.txt

reverie.title: REVERIE — the broadcast hour
narr: You and Leif sit in the equipment shed's dark, listening
to the broadcast tower rotate outside. Its hum rises and
falls. He says: 'It's been calling into nothing for so long,
maybe it's learned to hear itself.' You reach over and hold
his hand. The static in the speakers sounds almost like mercy.
Neither of you tries to answer. Listening is enough.
